newsitem.title: TUNISIA: Tunisia, Qatar sign deal for joint olive oil firm.
newsitem.headline: Tunisia, Qatar sign deal for joint olive oil firm.

text.p: Tunisia and Qatar have signed a deal for a joint company to market Tunisia's olive oil in the Mideast Gulf, a Tunisian official said on Monday.

Abdelhakim Mekadmi, Director general of the Tunisian state-run Office National de l'Huile (ONH), told Reuters the two countries would set up a company in Qatar that would start packaging Tunisian olive oil by 1998, with an objective of 1,000 tonnes the first year and 5,000 tonnes yearly later.
The Tunisian Qatari Food Industry Company would have a $1.5 million capital, 51 percent subscribed by Qatari public firms and 49 percent by Tunisian private companies and ONH.
"Our objective is to market the Tunisian olive oil in the member countries of the Gulf General Council from Qatar," Mekadmi said.
Olive oil is Tunisia's main food export.
The deal was signed over the weekend by Mekadmi and Hamad Saad al-Saad, chairman of the Qatari national company for industry, food and agriculture industrialisation.
The deal follows an agreement in principle announced in 1995 at the end of a visit to Tunisia by the Emir of Qatar, Sheikh Khalifa bin Hamad al-Thani.
